title: A Unified Theory of Electricity and Magnetism
attribution: Adapted (trimmed) from the Wikipedia article "Electrical engineering," available under CC BY-SA 4.0.
body: Electricity has been a subject of scientific interest since at least the early 17th century. William Gilbert was a prominent early electrical scientist, and was the first to draw a clear distinction between magnetism and static electricity. He is credited with establishing the term "electricity". He also designed the versorium: a device that detects the presence of statically charged objects. In 1762 Swedish professor Johan Wilcke invented a device later named electrophorus that produced a static electric charge. By 1800 Alessandro Volta had developed the voltaic pile, a forerunner of the electric battery.

In the 19th century, research into the subject started to intensify. Notable developments in this century include the work of Hans Christian Oersted, who discovered in 1820 that an electric current produces a magnetic field that will deflect a compass needle; of William Sturgeon, who in 1825 invented the electromagnet; of Joseph Henry and Edward Davy, who invented the electrical relay in 1835; of Georg Ohm, who in 1827 quantified the relationship between the electric current and potential difference in a conductor; of Michael Faraday, the discoverer of electromagnetic induction in 1831; and of James Clerk Maxwell, who in 1873 published a unified theory of electricity and magnetism in his treatise Electricity and Magnetism.

Practical applications and advances in such fields created an increasing need for standardized units of measure. They led to the international standardization of the units volt, ampere, coulomb, ohm, farad, and henry. This was achieved at an international conference in Chicago in 1893. The publication of these standards formed the basis of future advances in standardization in various industries.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who is credited with establishing the term "electricity"?
options: William Gilbert
Alessandro Volta
Michael Faraday
James Clerk Maxwell

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Gilbert's versorium detect?
options: The presence of statically charged objects
The strength of a magnetic field
The flow of electric current
The temperature of a conductor

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Volta develop by 1800?
options: The voltaic pile
The electromagnet
The electrical relay
The versorium

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Oersted discover in 1820?
options: That an electric current produces a magnetic field that deflects a compass needle
That magnetism and static electricity are identical
That electricity could be stored in a pile of metal discs
That heat could be converted directly into electricity

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Faraday discover in 1831?
options: Electromagnetic induction
The electrical relay
The voltaic pile
The unified theory of electricity and magnetism

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where was the international conference that standardized electrical units held?
options: Chicago
London
Paris
Berlin

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the author group Oersted, Sturgeon, Henry, Davy, Ohm, Faraday, and Maxwell together in one paragraph?
options: To show how rapidly scientific understanding of electricity and magnetism advanced throughout the 19th century
To argue that they all worked together in the same laboratory
To prove that only British scientists contributed to electrical theory
To explain why electricity was not studied before the 19th century

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did standardized units like the volt and ampere become necessary?
options: Practical applications and advances in the field created an increasing need for consistent measurement
Governments required all scientists to use the same language
Earlier scientists had refused to measure their results at all
The units were needed to settle a dispute between Volta and Gilbert

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the overall point of the passage?
options: Understanding of electricity developed gradually from early scientific curiosity into a rapidly advancing, eventually standardized field of study
Electricity was fully understood as early as the 17th century
Standardized units of measure existed long before electrical science began
Electrical engineering had no connection to earlier scientific discoveries

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that Ohm "quantified" the relationship between current and potential difference?
options: He expressed it in precise, measurable terms
He first discovered that a relationship existed
He disproved an earlier theory about the relationship
He gave the relationship its modern name

questions.prompt: According to the passage, in what year did Johan Wilcke invent the electrophorus?

options: The electromagnet
The voltaic pile
The electrical relay
The versorium

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who invented the electrical relay in 1835?
options: Joseph Henry and Edward Davy
Hans Christian Oersted
Georg Ohm
James Clerk Maxwell

questions.prompt: Per the passage, in what treatise did Maxwell publish his unified theory?
options: Electricity and Magnetism
Principles of Electrical Science
The Nature of Electric Force
On the Motion of Charged Bodies

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the publication of standardized units suggest about the state of electrical engineering by the 1890s?
options: It had matured into a field organized enough to require and adopt shared international measurement standards
It had stagnated since the early 19th century
It remained a purely theoretical pursuit with no practical use
It was rejected by most industries at the time

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes the passage's account of early electrical science?
options: Early scientists like Gilbert, Wilcke, and Volta laid the groundwork that 19th-century researchers rapidly built upon
Electrical science began and ended within the 19th century
Gilbert's work was later proven entirely incorrect
No progress was made in electrical science before 1893

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that Gilbert drew a "clear distinction" between magnetism and static electricity?
options: He showed they were separate, distinguishable phenomena
He proved they were the exact same phenomenon
He invented new words for both phenomena
He measured both phenomena using the same instrument
